note: REGIME: an energy-led tape inside a rate-hike scare, with AI hardware the one growth pocket still working. August CPI came in at 3.4% y/y against 3.3% expected and core rose 0.3% m/m, an acceleration from 0.2% - which pushed the odds of a 25bp hike at the Sep 16 FOMC to roughly 81-90%. It would be the Fed's first hike since 2023. The 10-year ended at 4.96% and the 2-year at 4.63%, so the curve is positively sloped, not inverted. The four-session week was down - Dow -1.6%, S&P -0.8%, Nasdaq -0.7% - but Friday snapped a four-day losing streak hard: S&P 7,656.98 (+0.86%), Dow 52,573.29 (+0.98%, +509.19pts), Nasdaq 26,333.04 (+0.96%), as Brent fell 2.5% to just under $105 on Hormuz diplomacy hopes and CPI landed close enough to expectations to calm the tape. Energy was the best sector for a second straight week with Brent +8.7% and WTI +9.4%; CVX printed a 52-week high at 214.06 on Sep 11, its second in three sessions, and COP and VLO hit highs on Sep 9 when Brent first settled above $101 since May. The refining complex was extraordinary - the WTI 3-2-1 crack cleared $64 against a $19 long-run median, and VLO, PSX, PBF, MPC, DINO and DK all made 52-week highs. Friday's leadership was Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary and Information Technology. The single biggest move was Oracle's Sep 10 print, which reaffirmed roughly $95bn of AI capex and named Dell and HPE: DELL +11.98% to a 52-week high of 567.29, HPE +12.44%, SMCI +7.28%, and a targeted networking rotation took ANET +5.61%, CSCO +3.1%, CIEN +4.5%, F5 +3.2%. Rotation: INTO energy, refining, AI hardware and networking; OUT of long-duration software, healthcare and the AI-power complex, which decoupled from AI capex - CEG -0.43% and VST only 11.9% above its 52-week low, and UBS cut NuScale to Sell with SMR -15.67%. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. spVs200 is an approximation.
